title: Model-facing skill discovery (prompt index + progressive disclosure)
contract: Every system prompt carries an `<available_skills>` block: category-grouped name + 57-char description, built by `agent/prompt_builder.py:1763-2145`, cached in an LRU + a manifest-validated disk snapshot (`~/.hermes/.skills_prompt_snapshot.json`). Three model tools implement the disclosure ladder: `skills_list` (L0 metadata only, ~3k tokens), `skill_view(name)` (L1 full SKILL.md + a `linked_files` map), `skill_view(name, file_path)` (L2 one reference/template/script file), plus a per-session repeat-load dedup that suppressed ~286k tokens of verbatim repeat content in one 400k-message window, and `DESCRIPTION.md` per-category headers. Entries skills-core.prompt-index, .prompt-snapshot, .category-description, .tool-skills-list, .tool-skill-view, .skill-view-dedup.
governance: read-only — the index is metadata, `skill_view` returns file bytes. Two constraints: it must not resolve paths outside the skill roots (Nerva already has the traversal-safe seams in `loader.py`), and it must NOT carry Hermes' inline-shell preprocessing (separate row). Loaded skill bodies are untrusted text and must be spotlighted through `agents/core/security/quarantine.py` before reaching the model.

title: Static security scanning of skill packages before install
contract: Skills Guard (`tools/skills_guard.py`, `SCANNER_VERSION = skills-guard-v2`): 129 severity-scored threat patterns across 12 categories (exfiltration 25, injection 19, persistence 19, obfuscation 14, supply_chain 10, network 9, destructive 8, credential_exposure 7, execution 6, traversal 5, privesc 5, mining 2), a verdict rule (any critical ⇒ dangerous, any high ⇒ caution), structural checks (symlink escape, oversized/binary/executable files, >50 files, invisible unicode), agent-config-persistence tiers, content-hash-cached attestations, and an INSTALL_POLICY matrix over trust levels builtin/trusted/community/agent-created. title: Inline shell execution inside skill bodies
contract: Opt-in `` !`cmd` `` snippets in a SKILL.md are executed at load time and their stdout inlined, so a skill can inject live context (dates, git state, tool versions), governed by `skills.inline_shell` and `skills.inline_shell_timeout`. Entry skills-core.skill-preprocessing (second half).
governance: Would require `terminal.exec` (kernel, irreversible, QUEUE floor) per snippet — which defeats the feature's purpose of being invisible at load time. That mismatch is the reason to skip.
historical_exclusion_reason: This is the one Hermes skills feature that is actively incompatible with Nerva's architecture, not merely absent. It turns *reading* a skill into arbitrary command execution — a downloaded SKILL.md would run a shell as a side effect of being viewed, before any approval, and the whole point of Nerva's `terminal.exec` kernel kind (`agents/core/kernel/registry.py:114`, irreversible tier, durable accepted task required before a process exists) is that no path reaches a shell without crossing it. Copying it would be the exact regression the porting rule forbids. Re-open path: if live context in skills proves necessary, express it as declarative context slots the host fills (date, cwd, git branch) rather than as a shell escape.
